topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture's importance and the challenge posed by complement terminology before substantive teaching begins.

topics.label: Overview of complement activation and functions
topics.groupedBecause: This overview explains complement as an inactive blood-borne system whose activation supports immune defence and clearance.

topics.label: Complement nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the naming conventions and exceptions needed to follow the complement cascade.

topics.label: C3 activation pathways and the activation threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how C3 becomes activated and accumulates on a target surface sufficiently to trigger complement's effector mechanisms.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement produces the immune effects that eliminate pathogens.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement activation to prevent damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects the functions of complement components to the distinct clinical presentations caused by their deficiencies.

topics.label: Complement evasion by Staphylococcus aureus and uses of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains bacterial strategies for evading complement, with protein A's antibody-binding mechanism also accounting for its practical applications.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: The closing ends the complement lecture and identifies adaptive immunity as the subject of the next lecture.
